gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-funnel-san: Electroharmonix splits every word into separate, open-handed letters with a loud, commanding streak. Funnel Sans keeps its strokes steady and its e pried open, giving all that drama somewhere tidy to rest.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-gafata: Gafata reads contemporary and tidy, with a tall band of letters. Electroharmonix cuts each word into striking separate letters, while the sans text below keeps its wide-eyed e's and short stalks in order.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-geist: Geist keeps a quiet, level beat with no accents of weight. Beside it, Electroharmonix feels like a shout in separate, open-handed letters, and the pairing gets its tension from that hush against all that swagger.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-georama: Electroharmonix splits every word into bold, separate, commanding letters. Georama then settles in with its bracelet-open c and barely rising capitals, so the page moves from shout to conversation.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-gidole: Gidole reads clean and level, every stroke drawn like neon tube. Its strokes never thicken or thin, which leaves Electroharmonix free to steal the spotlight with its gapped, open-handed letters.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-golos-text: Contemporary and approachable, Golos Text lets its x-height fill the line, built from a single stroke width. And while Electroharmonix is best at grabbing attention with split-up letters, Golos Text is best at carrying words steadily.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-hedvig-let: Gaps that break each word into single letters give Electroharmonix its commanding, striking look. And Hedvig Letters Sans gives that drama a friendly partner, its small letters standing almost as tall as capitals.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-heebo: Spaces that split each word into single letters make Electroharmonix hard to ignore. Heebo is the one built for steady reading, with a tall central band and curves that stop short of closing.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-hind-guntu: Hind Guntur reads modern, its lowercase standing tall like stamped metal type with no thick-thin shift. While Electroharmonix does the shouting through gapped, open-handed letters, Hind Guntur does the carrying, ring after ring of constant-walled o's.
gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-hind-madur: Approachable and plain-spoken, Hind Madurai fills the line with lowercase that stands like capitals and wide-open s curves. Loud gapped letters meet signage-plain text, and Electroharmonix gets to stay striking.
